director.chapterArc: Grief-stricken numbness transitions into pragmatic labor, then tense tactical negotiation with Rook's revelation about the fuel smell, ending in grim determination.
director.restraintNote: Maintain adult narrator distance; do not adopt Toren's teenage voice. Let silence carry the weight of death and the 'fuel' warning. Character voices are temporary color only.

cues.delivery: Internal monologue of Toren filtered through narrator. Subtext: The denial of a final goodbye is the true wound.
cues.from: He had spent the whole walk around the bend deciding what he would say, and the deciding had been the only thing holding him upright, and then he came round the rock, and there was nothing to say anything to. Garrick Voss was sitting with his back against the rock face where he had put it at the start, the brush axe across his knees. His eyes were open, looking at the far wall of the cut with mild interest, as though somebody had just told him a price he was considering.
cues.through: He wanted, badly, to have been given something. A sentence. A hand on the neck. Even a look. He was thirteen, and he had not yet learned that this is what everyone wants, and that almost nobody gets it. The last real thing his father had said to him had already happened, in a road cut, at a run, with the world coming apart: keep the ugly shape, stop trying to be good at it.
cues.reason: Toren's internal realization about his father's silence.

cues.delivery: Rook speaking to Milo. Subtext: Honoring the dead through brutal honesty rather than comfort.
cues.from: At the end he stood over Marta Faust's cairn and looked at Milo and said, "She held that wall while you had your hands on the old woman. She could have dropped it and turned round. She'd have had time. She didn't, because she'd told you not to lift your hands, and she wasn't going to make a liar of herself." He said it like a man reading a weight off a scale. "I don't know what she was to you. But that's what she did, and I watched her do it, and it's not going to sound better in a year."
cues.through: He turned around and went back to the cart, and Milo stood by the stones another minute and then followed him, and something in the boy had been set down a little differently than it had been before. Toren noticed it and did not know what to do with it.
cues.reason: Character dialogue for Rook regarding Marta's sacrifice.

cues.delivery: Senna speaking. Subtext: Commanding facts over comfort; voice hollowed out by injury.
cues.from: Senna was conscious and lucid by late afternoon and immediately became the worst patient anyone had ever had. Her left arm was strapped across her chest, and the shoulder was packed and bound, and she had been told four times not to use the hand.
cues.through: He said it. She listened, and then she looked away down the cut for a long moment at nothing, and then she said, "All right," in a voice that had had everything taken out of it, and asked for water, and drank it herself, with the wrong hand.
cues.reason: Character dialogue for Senna demanding news of her son.

cues.delivery: Toren searching the coat. Subtext: The comb is a physical anchor for grief; the shotgun without shells represents lost agency.
cues.from: Toren went through his father's coat because somebody had to and because he could not stand to have somebody else do it. There was: a folding knife. A flint. Three feet of waxed cord. Two dried apples. A bone comb that had been his mother's, which Toren had not known his father carried and which was the thing that finally broke him, out of everything, a comb. A folded paper with the Coldwater bridge tolls written on it in his father's blocky hand, and under that a column of numbers that Toren looked at for a while before he understood: days. His father had been counting the days to Meridian against something. Against Senna, probably. Against the road.
cues.through: "Right," Wyck said, and went away again, and came back ten minutes later with the shotgun Bram Sark had stood against the guardrail, and set it down on the tailgate where Toren could see it. There were no shells. Both of them knew there were no shells.
cues.reason: Narrative focus on Toren's discovery of the father's items.

cues.delivery: Rook explaining the fuel. Subtext: A mechanic reading data; no warmth, just survival necessity.
cues.from: The man's name came out at dusk, and it came out the way a splinter comes out — sideways, and only because someone kept at it.
cues.through: "Rook," he said, and walked past her.
cues.reason: Character dialogue for Rook defining the 'fuel' and his name.

cues.delivery: Dessa confronting Rook. Subtext: Cold logic cutting through the silence; forcing a truth that cannot be hidden.
cues.through: "Two days," he said. "To the wall. That is the whole thing I'm agreeing to, and I want all four of you to hear me say it, because I don't want an argument at the end of it. I walk you to Hobb's Wall. I put you in front of the people there. After that you are theirs, and you are not mine, and I have somewhere to be, and I have been late to it for a long time."
cues.reason: Character dialogue for Dessa challenging Rook's timeline.

cues.delivery: Rook giving final orders. Subtext: A reluctant protector establishing boundaries; the 'bill not yet due' look.
cues.from: Rook looked at him for a second longer than was comfortable. Then he picked up the cart shafts himself, on the near side, next to the mule, which was not a thing Toren had ever seen a grown man do, and said, "We're not sleeping in this cut. Two miles. Now, while there's light. Girl — Dessa — you're on the head. Boy with the bar, you're behind the cart, and you don't get to look at anything except behind the cart. Little one—"
cues.through: They went north out of the cut with the light going purple on the top of the western wall, and behind them the three cairns got smaller and then went round the bend and were not there any more, and Toren did not look back at them either, because he had decided somewhere in the last hour that he was going to be a person who did not look back, and it would take him most of a year to find out how poorly that particular decision worked.
cues.reason: Character dialogue for Rook assigning roles and warning Toren.

pauses.after: He had spent the whole walk around the bend deciding what he would say, and the deciding had been the only thing holding him upright, and then he came round the rock, and there was nothing to say anything to. Garrick Voss was sitting with his back against the rock face where he had put it at the start, the brush axe across his knees. His eyes were open, looking at the far wall of the cut with mild interest, as though somebody had just told him a price he was considering.
pauses.reason: Scene turn: The realization of death's finality before the physical act of closing eyes.

pauses.after: He closed his father's eyes, because he had seen it done, and it seemed to be a thing you did. It was harder than it looked. Then he sat down beside him on the road bed with his shoulder against the same rock and put his hands over his face and stayed there until Dessa came and got him.
pauses.reason: Emotional landing: Toren sitting in shock; a breath for the weight of grief.

pauses.after: There was plenty of it. The eastern wall had shed half a hillside into the cut over the decades, and it lay along the base in a long ridge, everything from head-sized down. They carried it. That was the afternoon: four young people and a man none of them knew, carrying rock two hundred paces up a road cut, one armload at a time, and laying it over three people until the shapes underneath stopped being shapes.
pauses.reason: Speaker reset/Scene turn: Transition from labor description to Rook's specific speech about Marta.

pauses.after: He turned around and went back to the cart, and Milo stood by the stones another minute and then followed him, and something in the boy had been set down a little differently than it had been before. Toren noticed it and did not know what to do with it.
pauses.reason: Thought completion: The shift in Milo's demeanor; a moment for the narrator to observe this change.

pauses.after: Nineteen, the last number said. Then it had been crossed out and eighteen written under it.
pauses.reason: Revelation: Toren realizing his father was counting days against Senna and time. A pause for processing the implication of '18'.
Tactical shift: The decision to carry the empty shotgun; a beat before Wyck takes it.
Speaker reset/Scene turn: Rook's name revealed. A pause for Dessa (and listener) to register the identity of this stranger.
Dramatic landing: The confirmation that 'It brings more.' Silence must carry the horror of attracting enemies.
Major emotional turn: Rook admitting they cannot reach safety. A pause for the group to absorb this fatal truth and Wyck's silence.

pauses.after: "You keep that thing in your hand," he said, "and you don't ask it for anything clever."
pauses.reason: Instructional weight: The warning about the Ember ('don't ask it for anything clever'). A pause before the final departure.
